claims.head: Sheltered vs. Exposed
claims.body: The Rangers keep dangerous shots away, but the Ducks give up a lot of them. The Rangers are one of the league’s best for preventing dangerous shots, and Anaheim is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should come at the Ducks’ net.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 40% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

NYR.head: Leaning the Rangers’ way
NYR.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Ducks can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

ANA.head: The Ducks start a half-step behind
ANA.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage. The Ducks’ best way to tip it is piling up shots.
